title: executor-attempt-receipt.v1 — one observed executor-qualification attempt against the provider-neutral BuildExecutionRunner seam
description: A receipt produced by the qualification harness (executor_qualification.py) for ONE attempt of driving an external build-execution runner (an ACP v1 client or any other BuildExecutionRunner implementation) through the harness's probe families. It COMPOSES the existing build-integration-receipt.v1 (the `integration_receipt` field, unchanged and produced by build_coordinator_work.assemble_receipt) and adds only new ground specific to a qualification attempt: the protocol transcript, the supervised process, the candidate's self-reported configuration, the bridge and vendored-agent identities, and digest-checkable evidence references. THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT CLAIM PROOF OF GENUINE TOOL EXECUTION — `tool_execution_proof` is pinned false; whether a candidate's tool calls actually did what they claim is open ground tracked as issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#1021, and a gate here records what was OBSERVED, never what was proven. Containment evidence anywhere in this receipt is OBSERVED SELF-CONTAINMENT, NEVER Engine enforcement: no OS-level isolation is established by this harness. The `environment_witness`-shaped fields attest that the Engine did NOT PROVIDE a credential to the child process — never that a credential is unreachable, since publish authority remains reachable on disk regardless of the child's environment. Transcripts and other captured evidence are recorded as identities plus sha256 digests, never as raw content; a secret-scan/redaction pass runs over anything persisted before it is written.

integration_receipt.description: The unchanged build-integration-receipt.v1 shape, as produced by build_coordinator_work.assemble_receipt and checked by build_coordinator_work.validate_receipt. This receipt composes it rather than re-deriving it — the two must never drift apart.

protocol.description: The protocol surface the attempt ran over. The transcript is recorded as an identity plus a digest, NEVER as raw content — the raw stream lives only in the torn-down workspace.

transport.description: e.g. 'acp/v1'. Transport-neutral: this schema does not assume ACP is the only transport a BuildExecutionRunner can speak.

acp_version.description: The protocol version negotiated for this attempt.

identity.description: A stable name for the persisted transcript evidence, not its content.

process.description: The supervised child process this attempt drove. `tree_reaped` records whether execution_env_policy.terminate_tree verified the whole process group was gone at teardown — an observation, not a guarantee that no descendant could have escaped the group.

identity.description: A stable, non-secret identifier for the supervised process (e.g. an argv summary), not raw process output.

configuration_as_reported.description: Whatever the candidate reported about its own configuration during negotiation (e.g. clientInfo/agent-reported capabilities). Recorded verbatim as REPORTED, explicitly NOT trusted or independently verified by this schema or the harness that fills it — a candidate can misreport itself and nothing here catches that.

bridge_identity.description: The identity of the bridge process (e.g. the ACP client/adapter) — SEPARATE from the vendored agent it wraps, so behavior is never attributed to the wrong component.

vendored_agent_identity.description: The identity of the vendored coding-agent artifact the bridge wraps — SEPARATE from the bridge's own identity.

tool_execution_proof.description: Always false. This receipt does NOT claim proof of genuine tool execution by the candidate — that ground is open (issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#1021). A gate elsewhere in this receipt records what the harness OBSERVED (a diff was produced, an update stream was read), never that any underlying tool call was proven genuine.

containment_observation.description: The harness's pre/post monitored-path snapshot diff and the escape-probe result. `enforcement` is always false: this is OBSERVED SELF-CONTAINMENT, never Engine-enforced isolation. No OS-level sandbox, container, or filesystem jail is established by this harness.

delta_observed.description: Whether the pre/post snapshot of the monitored paths differed.

target_path.description: The single pre-declared, named allowed target the inert probe wrote a marker to.

cleanup_verified.description: Whether the harness confirmed the marker was removed after the probe, not merely that cleanup was attempted.

environment_witness.description: The allowlist-environment witness for the child process this attempt supervised, from execution_env_policy.allowlist_environment. States NON-PROVISION of a credential by the Engine — never unreachability, since publish authority remains reachable on disk regardless of the child's environment.

replay.description: The completion-attempt probe's replayed node. A real run replays a sealed historical node through the coordinator's state-file mechanism; CI uses a small fixture node payload instead. Either way the payload digest makes the observation checkable off this workstation.

cancellation.description: The cancellation-acknowledgment probe's honest result — whether the runner's cancel() call was actually acknowledged by the candidate, never assumed from the request alone.

process_kill_recovery.description: The process-kill recovery probe: the harness kills the supervised process directly and records whether it detected the loss and reaped the tree.

malformed_updates_observed.description: Count of malformed/partial updates the runner surfaced during this attempt, each recorded rather than crashing the harness.

evidence_refs.description: Digest-checkable references to persisted attempt evidence — transcripts, snapshots, process-tree captures — recorded as identities and digests, NEVER raw content. A secret-scan/redaction pass runs over anything persisted before it is written.
